newsitem.title: USA: Texaco, Monterey in $1.4 bln merger.
newsitem.headline: Texaco, Monterey in $1.4 bln merger.

text.p: Texaco Inc and Monterey Resources Inc said Monday they have agreed to merge in a $1.4 billion stock-swap transaction.
Under terms of the agreement, Monterey shareholders will recieve $21 in Texaco common stock for each share held.
Texaco also will assume Monterey's existing debt of about $285 million, the companies said.
Monterey shares finished Friday New York Stock Exchange trade at 15-1/16, and had not yet traded early Monday since the stock was held for news dissemination.
Texaco shares added 1-1/4 to 111-1/4 in early-session NYSE trade.
Texaco said the transaction, subject to approval by regulatory agencies and Monterey shareholders, will add an estimated 385 million barrels of proved reserves to its U.S. base.

Upon consummation, expected within 90 days, the deal will immediately increase Texaco's California production by 54,000 barrels per day (bpd) to 180,000 bpd, with the potential for additional increases in the next few years, Texaco said.
"...The combination will enable us to capitalize on our heavy oil expertise to maximize the potential of these fields," according to Texaco Chairman and Chief Executive officer Peter I. Bijur.
Texaco is one of the traditional producers of Kern River crude which has API of 13.4 degrees.
Monterey's board is recommending the merger to its shareholders.
